purpose: Real Studio raycast measurements of the walkable ride/landing surfaces Whirlpool Waltz uses, per HANDOFF.md section 5.1 steps 3-4. Produced by docs/splashdown/probes/measure-course-sockets.server.luau in a real Play session on place 121997450145716.
methodology: For each source BasePart under the injected ServerStorage.SplashdownAuthoringSources.Kit: clone it (the exported Kit and Workspace.battle_stadium are both left untouched), anchor the clone, clear its imported PivotOffset, move it with no rotation change to an isolated point 12000 studs above the arena, then cast a grid of downward Raycasts (Enum.RaycastFilterType.Include, filtered to the clone only) from above its bounding box down through it. Each hit position is converted to the clone's own object space via CFrame:PointToObjectSpace, so every recorded coordinate is root-local and independent of where the source sits. Grid spacing is 0.5 studs with a 0.25-stud resample along the centre lines, where a round plate's hub hole and a pizza's missing wedges actually sit. Hit/miss counts and a 5-stud cell height map are recorded per asset; '.' in a cell map means no ray in that cell hit anything, i.e. a real hole or an off-footprint cell. Clones and scratch folders were destroyed immediately after each measurement.
hazardPieceSupportSource: obstacle_16_001 (pizza hub), obstacle_13_002 (carousel canopy), obstacle_14_001/obstacle_15_001/obstacle_26_001 (disc hubs), obstacle_8_001 (swing-panel axle), obstacle_27_001 (two-arm cross), obstacle_12_001 (cross spinner), obstacle_6_001 (dumbbell), door_002..door_007 (door slabs) and trampoline_3_001/002 (striped pad) are mounted mechanisms, not walkable surfaces. Their Support contact is the measured underside centre (0, -size.Y/2, 0) and their sub-part poses are root.CFrame:Inverse() * child.CFrame, both computed directly from the per-child size + cframe rows already recorded in docs/splashdown/evidence/inventory.json, exactly as course-sockets-ballbarrage.json did for the pilot's hazards. They are not re-raycast here.

obstacle_16_002.role: Pizza ride plate: the headline missing-wedge platform. The cell map shows the wedges are REAL holes, not a texture -- an entire band of cells through the middle of the plate and a second radial slot return no hits at all.
obstacle_16_002.note: 63% misses is dominated by the genuine missing wedges plus the round footprint inside a square bounding box; it is not measurement noise.

obstacle_13_001.role: Carousel ride deck. Solid round top at a uniform local Y 5.6 with no holes; the canopy obstacle_13_002 rides above it at a measured +16.1007 Y and is not walkable.
obstacle_13_001.note: Misses are the corners of the square bounding box outside the round deck, not holes: every in-footprint cell reports 5.6.

obstacle_15_002.note: One genuine hole cell at the plate centre (the hub bore) plus the bounding-box corners. The in-footprint top varies 1.5-2.0 because the mesh has raised radial ribs; 2.02 is the rib crest and 1.5 the recessed panel between ribs.

obstacle_26_002.role: Large disc ride plate, second colour variant.
obstacle_26_002.note: Measured independently and returned byte-identical hit/miss counts, footprint and cell map to obstacle_15_002; the two differ only by MeshId (707607271224 vs 728200145624) and colour. The map is not duplicated here.

obstacle_14_002.note: No interior hole: every in-footprint cell reports a hit. The 0.5-1.0 cells are the recessed mesh panels, the 1.2 cells the rim and ribs.

obstacle_8_002.role: Swing-panel deck (the flat rocking panel, NOT the paddlewheel: obstacle_24 is the paddlewheel and obstacle_8 is this panel).
obstacle_8_002.note: The panel is NOT flat: one edge row measures 2.0 and the body 0.5-1.3. The 2.0 row is a raised lip along the high-Z edge, so a rider stands on roughly local Y 1.3, not on topLocalY. AssetManifest records 1.3 as the walkable top and keeps 1.999 here as the measured extreme.

water_platform_001.role: Small round landing / hub deck. Selected as Whirlpool Waltz's finish hub.
water_platform_001.note: Effectively solid: 84 misses out of 5850 rays are bevel rays at the rounded rim. Top varies only 4.4-4.7.

octagon_002.role: Evaluated as the spiral hub deck and NOT selected.
octagon_002.cellMapOmitted: 62x62 cells, all in-footprint cells a uniform 5.6; omitted here for size.
octagon_002.reasonNotSelected: 309.8 studs across. The spiral's inner radius is 65 studs, so even a hub sized to the inner turn would need a uniform scale near 0.12, at which the deck is 37 studs but only 1.35 studs thick and its measured rim detail disappears. water_platform_001 is already 37.27 studs across at scale 1 with a solid measured top, so it is the hub instead and octagon_002 is not used.
